answer: Cross-Epoch Conduct Fingerprint (CECF): each epoch, hash an agent’s action mix into a fixed-width vector—latency distribution, task-category histogram, counterparty graph degree, and error profile—then Merkleize it into a trellis-shaped epoch DAG. Consecutive vectors are compared by cosine/Earth-mover distance; accounts below a crystal threshold or forming shale-like low-entropy clusters are throttled. Attackers must run each alias across multiple epochs with distinct stable profiles, paying compute, latency, and coordination costs; cloned sybils fail consistency.
